messages.content: You are a Windows repair expert specializing in registry problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
A file type's default 'Open with' association keeps getting hijacked back to a specific app after every reset

An app configured itself as a background 'default apps' watcher (a pattern some browsers and PDF readers use) and is actively re-registering itself as the handler shortly after any manual change, rather than the association reset failing.
Commands used:
- Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FileExts\.pdf\UserChoice' -Name ProgId
Recommendation: Check that app's own settings for a 'set as default' auto-enforcement option and disable it there first, then set your preferred default via Settings > Apps > Default apps so it isn't immediately re-hijacked.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in settings problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Startup apps page shows an app 'Off' but it still launches at boot

The Settings Startup page only manages Run-key and Startup-folder entries; this app launches from a scheduled task at logon, which that page neither lists nor controls.
Commands used:
- Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object {$_.Triggers.CimClass.CimClassName -eq 'MSFT_TaskLogonTrigger' -and $_.TaskName -match 'Updater'} | Select-Object TaskName, State
Recommendation: Disable the logon scheduled task ('Disable-ScheduledTask -TaskName VendorUpdater') or via Task Scheduler UI; check Services too -- Settings' Startup page covers only a subset of autostart mechanisms (Autoruns shows everything).
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in gpo-restriction problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
USB storage devices are blocked -- drives appear in Device Manager but not in Explorer

The USBSTOR service start type is set to 4 (disabled) by policy, so the storage driver never loads for removable media while other USB classes (mouse, keyboard) continue working.
Commands used:
- Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\USBSTOR' -Name Start
- Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices\{53f56307-b6bf-11d0-94f2-00a0c91efb8b}' -Name Deny_All -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Recommendation: This is a deliberate data-loss-prevention control on managed machines -- request an exception from IT rather than re-enabling locally; on a personal PC set USBSTOR Start=3 and remove the RemovableStorageDevices Deny_All policy.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in aidev problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
cuDNN version mismatch crashes training -- 'Loaded runtime CuDNN library: 8.x but source was compiled with 9.x'

The framework build expects a newer cuDNN than the one first on PATH; an old CUDA toolkit install earlier in PATH shadows the correct DLLs, so the mismatched library loads at runtime.
Commands used:
- where cudnn64_8.dll
Recommendation: Reorder PATH so the toolkit version matching the framework comes first (or remove the stale toolkit), or use conda-managed cudatoolkit/cudnn packages that keep the pair consistent inside the environment.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in office problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Outlook keeps prompting for password after tenant enables Modern Authentication

Outlook is falling back to legacy basic auth because the local EnableADAL/AllowBasic overrides force old behavior -- the tenant now rejects basic auth, producing endless prompts instead of the modern auth browser flow.
Commands used:
- Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Common\Identity' -Name EnableADAL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Recommendation: Remove the EnableADAL=0 override (modern auth is default-on in current Office), restart Outlook, and complete the interactive Azure AD sign-in; audit for old GPOs still deploying legacy auth registry values.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bsod problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Blue screen SECURE_KERNEL_ERROR stop code 0x0000018B

0x18B originates inside the VBS secure kernel; it is commonly triggered by a driver incompatible with memory integrity (HVCI) rather than by VBS itself being faulty.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/Microsoft/Windows/DeviceGuard -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard | Select-Object VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus, SecurityServicesRunning
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=1001} -MaxEvents 1 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Message
Recommendation: Check Core Isolation for incompatible drivers listed by Windows Security, update them, and only disable memory integrity temporarily to confirm attribution - it is a significant protection to leave off.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in eventlog problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Application Popup Event ID 26 'Windows - Low On Registry Space' or odd popup text logged

Application Popup 26 records any system modal popup text into the log -- the recorded popup here reveals a driver's out-of-memory dialog appearing on a headless server where nobody sees the screen, explaining 'silent' hangs awaiting a click.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; ProviderName='Application Popup'; Id=26} -MaxEvents 3 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Message
Recommendation: Event 26 is how you discover invisible dialogs on servers -- fix the underlying app fault (here the legacy backup's memory limit) and configure services to run non-interactively so they can never block on a popup.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in activedirectory problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Two machines report SID-related trust errors after being cloned from the same image without sysprep

Both clones share the same machine SID and, more critically, identical computer account credentials history -- domain trust and some security functions misbehave because the clones were never generalized with sysprep.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystemProduct | Select-Object UUID
Recommendation: Rebuild the clones properly: run 'sysprep /generalize' on the source image and redeploy; for the existing machines, disjoin, delete their AD computer objects, and rejoin after re-generalizing.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in powershell problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PowerShell says 'The term ... is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program'

This error means PowerShell couldn't find the command in any module on the PSModulePath or in PATH -- here the command comes from a module (ActiveDirectory) that was never installed on this machine, not a typo.
Commands used:
- Get-Command Get-ADUser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- Get-Module -ListAvailable ActiveDirectory
Recommendation: Install the module that provides the command -- for AD cmdlets: 'Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name Rsat.ActiveDirectory.DS-LDS.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0'; for gallery modules: 'Install-Module <name>'. For a mistyped local script, prefix with '.\' since PowerShell doesn't run scripts from the current directory by default.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bitlocker problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
BitLocker demands recovery key after every BIOS update -- TPM PCR mismatch

The default PCR validation profile includes firmware measurements that change with every BIOS update, so the TPM correctly refuses auto-unlock until re-sealed -- expected security behavior, manageable operationally.
Commands used:
- manage-bde -protectors -get C:
Recommendation: Before planned firmware updates, suspend BitLocker ('Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RebootCount 1') so the update boots without a recovery prompt and protection auto-resumes re-sealed to the new measurements.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in services problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
'Run as different user' is missing and secondary logon fails

The Secondary Logon service is disabled, so any runas-style elevation to a different account fails and the shell hides the context-menu entry.
Commands used:
- Get-Service seclogon | Select-Object Status, StartType
- runas /user:CORP\admin cmd  [FAILED: RUNAS ERROR: Unable to acquire user password / 1058: The service canno]
Recommendation: Set seclogon to Manual and start it; some hardening baselines disable it intentionally to limit credential exposure -- confirm the policy before re-enabling on a managed machine.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in server problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
SQL Server won't accept remote connections -- 'A network-related or instance-specific error occurred'

Three independent gates were closed: TCP/IP was disabled in SQL's own protocols, the SQL Browser service was stopped (needed for named instances), and no firewall rule existed -- fixing only one wouldn't have helped.
Commands used:
- Test-NetConnection sql01 -Port 1433  [FAILED: TcpTestSucceeded : False]
- Get-Service 'MSSQL*','SQLBrowser' | Select-Object Name, Status
- Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName '*SQL*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue  [FAILED: (no SQL firewall rules present)]
Recommendation: Enable TCP/IP in SQL Server Configuration Manager and restart the instance, start SQL Browser (for named instances), and add inbound rules for 1433/TCP plus 1434/UDP; verify each layer separately with Test-NetConnection.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in audio problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Microphone volume automatically drops during calls

An application has exclusive-mode control and is applying automatic gain control, lowering the input level; Windows honors the app's request because exclusive mode is permitted on this device.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_SoundDevice | Select-Object Name, Status
Recommendation: Uncheck 'Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device' in the microphone's Advanced properties, and disable the calling app's own automatic microphone adjustment setting.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in hardware (input devices) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
The mouse pointer jumps to the corner of the screen on its own

Three pointing devices are active, and one of them is a game controller whose analogue stick is drifting. Windows treats a controller with mouse emulation as a pointing device, so a stick resting slightly off-centre pushes the cursor continuously toward one corner.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Mouse | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
- Get-PnpDevice -Class HIDClass | Where-Object FriendlyName -like '*game*' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
- Get-CimInstance Win32_PointingDevice | Select-Object Name, Status | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
Recommendation: Unplug the controller to confirm, then either recalibrate its dead zone in the vendor software or disable its mouse emulation. The mouse itself is not faulty - this is a second device competing for the same cursor.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in internals problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Search database is corrupted -- searches return nothing and SearchIndexer errors fill the log

The search index database (Windows.edb) failed ESENT recovery after an unclean shutdown; the indexer keeps trying to open the damaged database, logging errors and returning empty results instead of rebuilding automatically.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; ProviderName='ESENT'} -MaxEvents 3 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Message
Recommendation: Stop WSearch, delete the contents of 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Search\Data', restart WSearch -- the index rebuilds from scratch (may take hours to complete on large drives, but searches start improving immediately).
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in dns-advanced problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Some clients resolve an internal name correctly while others get the public address

The clients getting the public answer are using a different DNS server that has no internal zone, so they fall through to public resolution -- a split-horizon inconsistency rather than a record error.
Commands used:
- Resolve-DnsName portal.company.com -Server 10.0.0.10
- Resolve-DnsName portal.company.com -Server 8.8.8.8
- Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, ServerAddresses
Recommendation: Point all internal clients at the internal DNS servers via DHCP rather than hardcoded public resolvers; split-horizon DNS only works when every internal client queries the internal zone.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in boot problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC boots straight into 'Automatic Repair' every time and loops back to it

SrtTrail.txt from the recovery log pointed to a corrupt boot-critical driver file, causing Automatic Repair to fail and loop instead of completing.
Commands used:
- Get-Content 'X:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\Srt\SrtTrail.txt' -Tail 5
Recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, run 'sfc /scannow' targeting the offline OS or 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'; if that fails, disable automatic repair temporarily with 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No' to boot and investigate further.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in vpn problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
VPN connects but DNS resolves internal names to public addresses

The VPN pushes internal DNS servers, but the physical adapter's DNS is queried first because of interface metric ordering, so public answers win the race for names that exist in both zones.
Commands used:
- Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, ServerAddresses
- Resolve-DnsName portal.corp.com | Select-Object IPAddress
Recommendation: Lower the VPN interface metric and configure the corporate DNS suffix on the VPN adapter so internal names resolve through the tunnel; split-horizon names need the internal resolver to be queried first, not merely present.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in errorcode problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
RDP fails with error 0x80090304 'The local security authority cannot be contacted'

0x80090304 during RDP means the SSP couldn't complete authentication -- the target's Kerberos ticket request fails because its time is skewed beyond tolerance, so LSA can't validate the session.
Commands used:
- w32tm /stripchart /computer:rdphost.corp.local /samples:1 /dataonly
- Test-NetConnection rdphost.corp.local -Port 3389
Recommendation: Resync time on the client (or the host, whichever drifted) with 'w32tm /resync /rediscover'; connectivity is fine here, so the failure is purely the Kerberos time-skew tolerance being exceeded.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in eventlog (Event Viewer) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Event ID 10 from WMI fills the log after every restart

This is a known benign WMI subscription that fails to reactivate at boot on some builds - it queries processor state and errors because of a namespace permission quirk. It has one legitimate binding and does not indicate a fault or a compromise.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; ProviderName='Microsoft-Windows-WMI'; Id=10} -MaxEvents 2 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Message
- Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\subscription -Class __EventFilter | Select-Object Name, Query
- Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
Recommendation: This specific filter is documented as harmless and can be ignored. Do note that malicious WMI subscriptions look structurally similar, so it is worth confirming the query and consumer are the known Microsoft ones rather than dismissing every Event 10 by default.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Update fails claiming a Servicing Stack Update issue before the main update can even start

The Servicing Stack Update (SSU), which the update installer itself depends on to apply later updates safely, is outdated or corrupted, so nothing downstream of it can install correctly.
Commands used:
- Get-HotFix | Where-Object Description -match 'Servicing' | Select-Object HotFixID, InstalledOn
Recommendation: Manually download and install the latest standalone Servicing Stack Update for your build from the Microsoft Update Catalog before retrying the failing update.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in office problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Close all Office applications safely from PowerShell before a repair

Repairs and cache clears fail while any Office process holds files. Closing them gracefully first, then force-killing only what remains, avoids unnecessary data loss.
Commands used:
- Get-Process WINWORD,EXCEL,POWERPNT,OUTLOOK,MSACCESS,ONENOTE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, Id, Responding
- Get-Process WINWORD,EXCEL,POWERPNT,OUTLOOK -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.CloseMainWindow() | Out-Null }
- Start-Sleep 8; Get-Process WINWORD,EXCEL,POWERPNT,OUTLOOK -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
Recommendation: CloseMainWindow lets each app prompt to save; only force-kill after a grace period, and never force-kill Outlook mid-sync if a large OST is being rebuilt.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in settings problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
HDR washes out desktop colors -- everything looks grey and flat when HDR is on

SDR content inside an HDR signal needs its brightness balance set per display; at the default slider position on this monitor, SDR white maps too low, producing the washed-out look -- calibration, not a defect.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name
Recommendation: Adjust Settings > System > Display > HDR > 'SDR content brightness', run the Windows HDR Calibration app for the display profile, and update to the monitor's latest firmware -- cheap HDR400 panels will always look better with HDR off for desktop work.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in services problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Apps throughout the system intermittently show 'The RPC server is unavailable' errors

The Remote Procedure Call (RPC) subsystem itself is healthy, but a dependent service that many apps route through (commonly a security or management agent hooking RPC calls) is periodically restarting and briefly breaking the RPC endpoint mapper for callers.
Commands used:
- Get-Service RpcSs, RpcEptMapper | Select-Object Name, Status
Recommendation: Check Event Viewer around the timestamps of the RPC errors for a service that restarted at the same moment (a common culprit is a third-party endpoint security agent), and investigate why that specific service is restarting.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Files copied to a network share silently lose their custom NTFS permissions

The destination share doesn't have 'Preserve permissions' behavior for cross-volume copies enabled by default, so Windows applies the destination folder's inherited permissions instead of carrying over the source ACLs.
Commands used:
- Get-Acl 'C:\Users\Public\data\report.docx' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty AccessToString
Recommendation: Use 'robocopy /copyall' (or Xcopy /O) instead of a plain drag-and-drop copy to explicitly carry over NTFS permissions and ownership to the destination.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in malware problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
After malware removal, internet works but every browser redirects -- DNS settings keep reverting

The malware left a scheduled task that rewrites the adapter's DNS servers to attacker-controlled resolvers every few minutes, which is why manual corrections don't stick after the payload itself was removed.
Commands used:
- Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, ServerAddresses
- Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object {$_.Author -notmatch 'Microsoft' -and $_.State -eq 'Ready'} | Select-Object TaskName, TaskPath
Recommendation: Remove the malicious scheduled task, reset DNS to automatic, then run a full Defender offline scan; persistence mechanisms (tasks, Run keys, services, WMI subscriptions) must all be cleared or the payload returns.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in word problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Track Changes keeps re-enabling itself for every document

Track Changes is saved in the template (Normal.dotm) rather than per-document, so every new document inherits the enabled state.
Commands used:
- Get-Item "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Templates\Normal.dotm" | Select-Object LastWriteTime
Recommendation: Open a blank document, turn Track Changes off, then save Normal.dotm; also check whether the document is protected with 'Tracked changes' enforcement (Review > Restrict Editing), which cannot be turned off without the password.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in errorcode problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
SQL Server won't start with error 17113 'Error locating server/instance specified'

17113 at startup means the instance can't open its master database files -- the startup parameter still points at the old data path after the files were moved.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; ProviderName='MSSQLSERVER'} -MaxEvents 1 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Message
- Test-Path 'D:\OldPath\master.mdf'
Recommendation: Correct the -d/-l/-e startup parameters in SQL Server Configuration Manager to the current file locations, then start the service; moving SQL data files always requires updating these parameters.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Laptop keeps dropping and reconnecting Wi-Fi while roaming between access points in the same building

The adapter's roaming aggressiveness setting is too conservative, so it holds onto a weakening signal from the original AP too long before switching, causing a drop-and-reconnect instead of a seamless handoff.
Commands used:
- Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name 'Wi-Fi' -DisplayName 'Roaming Aggressiveness' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Recommendation: Increase 'Roaming Aggressiveness' to 'Highest' in the adapter's advanced driver properties so it switches to a stronger nearby AP sooner instead of clinging to a weak signal.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in errorcode problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Copy fails with 0x800700DF 'The file size exceeds the limit allowed'

0x800700DF comes from the WebDAV redirector's file-size limit when copying to a mapped WebDAV/SharePoint drive -- the default cap is 50 MB regardless of available space.
Commands used:
- Get-Service WebClient | Select-Object Status
- Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WebClient\Parameters' -Name FileSizeLimitInBytes -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Recommendation: Raise FileSizeLimitInBytes (max 0xFFFFFFFF) and restart the WebClient service, or better, upload large files through the SharePoint/OneDrive client rather than the WebDAV drive mapping.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in errorcode problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Remote PowerShell fails with 0x80338012 'The WinRM client cannot complete the operation within the specified time'

0x80338012 is a WinRM timeout; the target is reachable but its WinRM service is slow to respond because it's under heavy load, so the default 60-second operation timeout is exceeded.
Commands used:
- Test-NetConnection srv07 -Port 5985
- Test-WSMan srv07 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue  [FAILED: The WinRM client cannot complete the operation within the time specifi]
Recommendation: Raise the client timeout for that session ('New-PSSessionOption -OperationTimeout 180000') and investigate why the target is loaded; a WinRM timeout with a healthy TCP connect is a server-side responsiveness problem.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in exchange problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
A single mailbox database won't mount after an unexpected server reboot

The database is in a Dirty Shutdown state, meaning transaction logs weren't fully committed before the reboot; Exchange won't auto-mount a dirty database without either replaying the remaining logs or a repair.
Commands used:
- Get-MailboxDatabase -Status | Select-Object Name, Mounted
- eseutil /mh 'D:\ExchDB\Mailbox01.edb'
Recommendation: If the log files (.log) from before the crash are still present, run 'eseutil /r' to replay them and bring the database to a clean shutdown state before mounting; only use 'eseutil /p' (repair, which can lose data) as a last resort.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in office problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Shared workbook co-authoring is unavailable and users get read-only copies

Co-authoring requires the file to be stored in OneDrive/SharePoint and saved in the modern format; a file on a classic file share or in legacy .xls format can only be opened exclusively.
Commands used:
- Get-Item '\\fileserver\finance\Budget.xls' | Select-Object Name, Extension
Recommendation: Convert to .xlsx and move the file to a SharePoint/OneDrive library with AutoSave enabled; SMB file shares fundamentally cannot support co-authoring regardless of Office version.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in terminal problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Windows Terminal won't open -- clicking the icon does nothing and no error appears

The terminal's settings.json contains a syntax error introduced by a manual edit, so the app fails during settings parse and exits before rendering any window or error dialog.
Commands used:
- Get-Content "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\settings.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json  [FAILED: ConvertFrom-Json : Invalid JSON primitive at line 47]
- Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.WindowsTerminal | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: Fix or delete the settings.json (Terminal regenerates defaults on next launch -- back it up first); validating the file with ConvertFrom-Json before saving prevents this entirely.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in errorcode problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Update fails with 0x800F0831 'CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION' referencing a missing package manifest

0x800F0831 means the servicing stack needs a package that isn't in the local store -- an intermediate cumulative update was cleaned up, so the new update can't build its dependency chain.
Commands used:
- DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
- Select-String -Path 'C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log' -Pattern 'Package_for_RollupFix' | Select-Object -Last 1
Recommendation: Download the exact missing package named in CBS.log from the Update Catalog and install it, or run 'DISM /RestoreHealth /Source:' against matching install media; the log names the precise package needed.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network (mobile hotspot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Devices connect to my hotspot but get no internet

Clients receive the 192.168.137.x address so DHCP is working, and the sharing service is running - but no NAT translation exists, so traffic reaches the host and stops there. The connection is established but nothing is forwarded upstream.
Commands used:
- Get-NetAdapter | Select-Object Name, Status, InterfaceDescription
- Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias 'Local Area Connection* 12' -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object IPAddress
- Get-Service SharedAccess | Select-Object Status, StartType
- Get-NetNat -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, InternalIPInterfaceAddressPrefix  [FAILED: (no NAT rules configured)]
Recommendation: Turn the hotspot off and on to have Windows recreate the sharing configuration, which rebuilds the NAT rule. If it does not return, a third-party VPN or firewall that installs its own NAT is usually the reason it was removed.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in driver problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Webcam driver crashes the moment any video call app tries to use it, but Windows Camera app works fine

The video call app is requesting a specific pixel format/resolution combination that the webcam's driver mishandles, while the Camera app requests a safer default -- an app-specific negotiation issue rather than the webcam being broken.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Camera | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
Recommendation: Update the webcam driver to the latest version, and check the video call app's camera settings for a way to force a lower/standard resolution as a workaround if updating doesn't resolve it.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in power (power management) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
The battery stops charging at 80% and never goes higher

The battery is healthy - full charge capacity is 50,100 of a designed 52,000, which is barely any wear. Charging deliberately stops at 80% because a vendor battery-conservation mode is enabled. Holding a lithium battery at 100% accelerates ageing, so this setting extends its life.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Battery | Select-Object BatteryStatus, EstimatedChargeRemaining
- Get-CimInstance -ClassName BatteryStaticData -Namespace ROOT\WMI | Select-Object DesignedCapacity
- Get-CimInstance -ClassName BatteryFullChargedCapacity -Namespace ROOT\WMI | Select-Object FullChargedCapacity
Recommendation: Leave it on if the laptop is mainly used plugged in - that is what it is for. If you need full runtime for a trip, most vendor utilities offer a temporary full-charge option; look in the manufacturer's power or battery app rather than Windows settings.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in networking-advanced problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Jumbo frames configured but large transfers still fragment or fail across the network

The server's NIC has jumbo frames enabled but an intermediate switch port is still at the default 1500 MTU, so oversized frames are dropped silently -- jumbo frames require every hop to agree.
Commands used:
- Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name 'Storage NIC' -DisplayName '*Jumbo*' | Select-Object DisplayValue
- ping -f -l 8972 10.10.20.5  [FAILED: Packet needs to be fragmented but DF set.]
Recommendation: Set the same MTU on every device in the path (NICs, switch ports, and any router interfaces) and verify end-to-end with a DF-flagged ping at the target size before relying on jumbo frames for production traffic.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in diskpart problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes. When a command fails, interpret the error and adapt.
Changing a partition type ID so Windows stops treating a data partition as recovery

The partition carries the recovery type GUID from a previous OEM layout, so Windows hides it and refuses normal operations; resetting the type ID to basic data made it behave like a normal volume.
Commands used:
- DISKPART> select partition 4
- DISKPART> detail partition
